newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-SKRELA UPBEAT DESPITE FRENCH INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SKRELA UPBEAT DESPITE FRENCH INJURIES.

text.p: France hope to rise above their current injury crisis when a reshuffled team containing six enforced changes meet Wales in the Five Nations championship at Parc des Princes on Saturday.

The injured Emile N'Tamack, Thomas Castaignede, Alain Penaud, Fabien Galthie and Philippe Benetton, plus suspended prop Franck Tournaire, were replaced by Bourgoin winger Laurent Leflamand, Dax centre Richard Dourthe, Brive half-backs Christophe Lamaison and Philippe Carbonneau, Beziers flanker Richard Castel and Toulouse prop Jean-Louis Jordana in the team announced on Wednesday.

"A few days ago, we were really worried but from what we saw in the last few practice sessions, we really think we can do well." said coach Jean-Claude Skrela, who has suffered huge disruption to his plans since France beat Ireland 32-15 on January 18.

Castaignede and Benetton have both suffered broken jaws in French domestic rugby, N'Tamack has a groin injury, Galthie tore knee ligaments against Ireland and Penaud hurt an ankle in leading Brive to their convincing victory in the European Cup final in Cardiff.
Tournaire, meanwhile, was banned from consideration for the Welsh game after video evidence showed he kicked replacement Irish hooker Allen Clarke in the head.
Skrela was pleased with France's defence and ball-winning capacity in Dublin but wants his reshaped back division to show more of a cutting edge.

"We must not drop as many balls as we did in that match and we must also show more initiative in running the ball," he said, adding he expected Wales to improve on their losing display against the Irish in Cardiff.
"Against Ireland, they used the wrong tactics," he said. "But they are an exciting team with strong forwards and gifted backs, a bit like us actually. It should be a great match to watch."

Team: 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny: 14-Laurent Leflamand, 13-Richard Dourthe, 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Venditti; 10-Christophe Lamaison, 9-Philippe Carbonneau; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Abdel Benazzi (captain), 6-Richard Castel, 5-Hugues Miorin, 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Jean-Louis Jordana, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Christian Califano.
Subs: 16-David Aucagne, 17-Sebastien Viars, 18-Guy Accoceberry, 19-Olivier Magne, 20-Pierre Triep Capdevielle, 21-Marc de Rougemont.
